title: Skill directories for Ravel 2.0.0
intro: Directory delivery from local sources on the skill-directory-delivery line. The local stage is implemented, and acceptance remains ahead. Graph views start at the dark node labelled Start here, and numbered edge labels give the order of steps. The sequence starts at its first message. Ravel supplies directories, and the agent finds the skills. The specification docs/specs/skill-discovery.md is the authority for every rule drawn here.

discussion.title: Keep each default source intact
discussion.status: Added by Grove's ravel-packaging-guidance-k301 on 2026-11-11, before the 2.0.0 cut. The rule binds packages. Ravel's resolver does not change
discussion.summary: A package installs each source as a private payload and exposes it through a relative directory symlink, the source alias. With Homebrew, the payload is libexec/skill-sources/ID in the keg and the alias is share/ravel/skills/ID. A real source directory under share can expand into links to its individual files when a later keg links into the same directory. Those links leave the source boundary, and Ravel refuses the whole resolution. Homebrew links an alias as one entry and never enters the payload.

updatedDiagrams.summary: The keg now holds a private payload and a source alias. The entry links to the alias, another keg leaves it one entry, and originPath names the payload.

diagrams.title: Prepare before the worker launches
diagrams.caption: An empty source set means no preamble and no cache work. Without sources in the settings, the default skill directory supplies the set. A source failure refuses at stage skills, before the worker launches. The script puts request.prompt into the harness arguments and reads request.originalPrompt for task analysis. Mandatory reads precede caller actions, and callers qualify first accordingly.

diagrams.title: Homebrew fills the directory
diagrams.caption: Ravel's formula writes the record with the prefix of that Homebrew installation, so a keg-only ravel@2, a Linux prefix and a Cellar inside the repository all name the right directory. Each skill formula installs a private payload and a source alias, so conflict repair for another keg leaves the source intact. Homebrew unlinks the earlier keg before it installs the new one. A launch in that interval delivers the other sources and refuses nothing, and a rerun captures the new keg.

diagrams.title: Choose the source set
diagrams.caption: Explicit sources replace the default, so "sources": [] turns it off. Without sources, the installation record beside the canonical executable names the default skill directory, and each entry is one source with the roots skills and craft that exist. An absent record or directory gives an empty set and refuses nothing. A malformed record or entry refuses before capture. A mandatory reference to an absent default source refuses as skill_source_missing.

diagrams.title: Where the prompt travels and which bound applies
diagrams.caption: The evaluate-frame bound is the sum of the public bounds at the largest JSON escape, so a request within those bounds fits. Ravel does not bound the kind, the working directory or the task-file path, so an exceptional value refuses as malformed_input before evaluation. The script result keeps its 1 MiB bound, and the platform argument limit can refuse less at launch.

diagrams.title: Keep the reader's directories
diagrams.caption: RAVEL_SKILL_DIRECTORIES keeps the same descriptor path, but it cannot keep an instruction to recover it. Whole-preamble loss needs an unprompted harness trial. Detached readers can outlive the managed group, and manual removal requires every affected reader to stop.

diagrams.title: Read resources under the harness sandbox and state the authority limit
diagrams.caption: The managed harness and each harness run receive the same absolute paths. Ravel applies no confinement, so the harness sandbox that the configuration script selects decides what each can read and write. A source that overlaps a protected path refuses before capture. Ordinary delegates can inherit the result context, and the instructions forbid them to use it. An adapter that controls the environment and the filesystem access removes that context, and a trial measures its isolation. Ravel cannot intercept arbitrary delegation interfaces of a harness.
